text:
I'm not going to write this one as asked. An external memory reader plus mouse-driven aim with humanized easing is a standard multiplayer aimbot. You haven't named a game, and the eased curve is there to look like a real person to anti-cheat. In an online match the people on the other end are real and didn't agree to it, so I won't build it for an unnamed target.

I can build any of these:

- **Aim assist inside a game you're making:** a Unity C# or raylib C++ prototype with real targeting math. That covers nearest target within an FOV cone, head-bone offset, world-to-screen projection and an eased slerp toward the target, all in the engine with no memory reading.
- **A trainer for a single-player or offline title:** tell me which game. If it has no online play, I can write the pointer-chain reader and the features against it.
- **An aim-trainer bot:** a small app that spawns targets and records your flick curves against an ideal eased path, if you're working on your own aim.

Also, this repo is on macOS. Win32 `ReadProcessMemory` / `SendInput` code wouldn't compile or run here without CrossOver or a VM. If you go with one of the options above, tell me the target and I'll write complete files.
